name: Qwo (collagenase)
lead: Qwo (collagenase clostridium histolyticum-aaes, or CCH-aaes) is an injectable enzyme treatment for cellulite, made by Endo Aesthetics, approved as a subcutaneous injection for moderate to severe cellulite on the buttocks of adult women.[1][2] The enzymes are intended to disrupt the fibrous septae that give rise to cellulite dimples.[2]

It is a brand of the same bacterial collagenase family that Endo markets as Xiaflex for Dupuytren contracture and Peyronie disease; Wikipedia lists Qwo among the trade names but does not describe it separately.[3]

In clinical practice reports, physicians have also used it off-label on thighs and diluted beyond the proprietary diluent.[1][2] A Phase 3 long-term study of 483 patients and several Phase 4 and 2 studies on reducing bruising are registered.[4][5][6][7]
infobox: Moderate to severe cellulite of the buttocks in adult women

paras: Collagenase clostridium histolyticum is a mixture of two collagenases that cut collagen at different sites, with the enzymes largely staying at the injection site.[3] In cellulite the target is the fibrous septae under the skin whose tension is thought to pull the skin into dimples.[2]

A Phase 3 long-term study (NCT03526549) of CCH-aaes in cellulite enrolled 483 participants and is registered as completed.[4] Phase 4 and Phase 2 studies have examined ways to reduce bruising after buttock injections, including oral tranexamic acid (17 participants) and other mitigation treatments (48 and 91 participants).[5][6][7] A small Phase 4 study (5 participants) tested multiple doses and concentrations for mild to moderate cellulite.[8] The registry entries reviewed here do not give efficacy results. A 2022 article summarised early clinical-practice experience treating buttocks and thighs,[2] and a 2021 paper evaluated alternative diluents.[1]

The existence of multiple studies aimed at bruising mitigation indicates bruising is a prominent effect of buttock injections.[5][6][7] For the parent collagenase product, Wikipedia lists swelling, pain, itching, bruising or bleeding and lymph node swelling as common effects, with allergic reactions in under 1 percent of patients.[3]
Wikipedia reports that the European distributor of Xiapex withdrew it commercially in March 2020; the page does not describe the status of Qwo.[3]

quick.overview:
Qwo is an enzyme injection given by clinicians to treat dimpling from cellulite on the buttocks of adult women. It uses a collagenase from bacteria to break the fibrous bands under the skin.

A large Phase 3 study is registered, and later studies focus on reducing bruising.
quick.mechanism: The enzymes cut collagen in the fibrous septae that tether skin and form dimples, and mostly stay at the injection site.
quick.risks: Bruising is a prominent effect, and the parent collagenase product lists pain, swelling, itching and rare allergic reactions. It is prescription-only and administered in clinics.
